newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli share funds post 3.4 pct February return.
newsitem.headline: Israeli share funds post 3.4 pct February return.

text.p: Israel mutual share funds averaged a 3.4 percent return in February, a sharp slowdown from their 15.3 percent return the previous month, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Sunday.
Meitav said the funds underperformed the market. The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's general share index rose 4.4 percent in February.
Meitav's index of all mutual funds rose 2.1 percent in the month, led by the relatively high returns on share funds. The average return for bonds funds was 1.8 percent for the month.

Because of the strong performance in January, Meitav said its mutual fund index had risen 9.3 percent in the first two months of the year, with all 310 funds included in its survey showing returns after inflation. Share funds rose 19.2 percent, it added.

Meitav, a brokerage and mutual fund manager that tracks the mutual fund industry, attributed the continued rally in Israeli share prices in February to increased foreign investment in blue chips and a flow of domestic liquidity into small capitalisation stocks.
"Towards the end of the month, after political developments in the Bar-On affair and the drop in Wall Street prices, declines were registered that erased half the monthly rise," Meitav said.
"These (two factors) in fact provided a rationale for the technical correction that was in any case required of the stock market," Meitav said.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and officials in his government are being questioned by police in connection with charges that the short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general was part of a deal for a plea bargain in the corruption trial of Aryeh Deri, a key figure in the governing coalition.

Meitav added that bond prices were weighed down by the small 0.3 percentage point reduction in interest rates announced by the bank of israel at the end of February and expectations for higher inflation in coming months.
